name: Hamilton
governance_summary: Hamilton voters elect a mayor and 15 city councillors who together form the 16-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of 15 wards. Elections are held every four years under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act, most recently on October 24, 2022, with the next election scheduled for October 26, 2026.

name: Brampton
governance_summary: Brampton voters elect a Mayor and councillors across 10 wards that form the city's elected council. The 10 wards are grouped into 5 pairs; each ward pair elects one City Councillor and one Regional Councillor (who sits on Peel Regional Council), for a total of 10 councillors. The Mayor is elected city-wide.

name: Toronto
governance_summary: Toronto voters elect a Mayor city-wide and one Councillor per ward across 25 wards, together forming the 26-member Toronto City Council. The council structure is established under the City of Toronto Act, 2006, which provides Toronto with a strong-mayor framework alongside the ward-elected council. Municipal elections are held every four years on the fourth Monday in October under the Municipal Elections Act, 1996.

name: Ottawa
governance_summary: Ottawa voters elect a Mayor city-wide and 24 ward councillors, one per ward, who together form the 25-member Ottawa City Council. Council operates on a non-partisan basis under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act, with elections held every four years on the last Monday of October.

name: Mississauga
governance_summary: Mississauga voters elect a mayor and 11 city councillors who together form the 12-member City Council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of 11 wards. Elections are held every four years under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act.

name: Barrie
governance_summary: Barrie voters elect a Mayor city-wide and one Councillor per ward across 10 wards, together forming the 11-member Barrie City Council. Council operates on a non-partisan basis under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act, with elections held every four years on the fourth Monday in October, most recently on October 24, 2022, with the next election scheduled for October 26, 2026.

name: Brantford
governance_summary: Brantford voters elect a Mayor city-wide and two Councillors per ward across five wards, together forming the 11-member Brantford City Council. Each of the five wards elects two councillors, for a total of 10 ward councillors alongside the Mayor. Council operates on a non-partisan basis under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act, with elections held every four years, most recently on October 24, 2022, with the next election scheduled for October 26, 2026.

name: County of Brant
governance_summary: The County of Brant is divided into five wards, each represented by two elected councillors, together with a Mayor elected county-wide forming an 11-member council. Elections are held every four years under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act, most recently on October 24, 2022, with the next election scheduled for October 26, 2026.

name: Ontario
governance_summary: Ontario voters elect 124 Members of Provincial Parliament (MPPs), each representing one of 124 provincial electoral districts, who together form the Legislative Assembly of Ontario. The Premier leads the government and is supported by a cabinet of ministers; the current 44th Parliament, elected on February 27, 2025, holds 42 role-scoped cabinet positions including the Premier, Deputy Premier, and ministers.

name: Canada
governance_summary: Canada is divided into 343 electoral districts (ridings), each electing one Member of Parliament by single-member plurality. The party or coalition commanding the confidence of the House of Commons forms the Government; its leader serves as Prime Minister. Federal elections are held on a fixed date (third Monday of October in the fourth calendar year after the previous election) under the Canada Elections Act, unless the House is dissolved earlier.

name: Guelph
governance_summary: Guelph voters elect a mayor city-wide and two councillors per ward across the city's six wards, together forming the 13-member Guelph City Council. Members of Council are elected to a four-year term of office under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act, most recently on October 24, 2022, with the next election scheduled for October 26, 2026.

name: Chatham-Kent
governance_summary: The Municipality of Chatham-Kent elects a mayor city-wide and 17 councillors across 6 wards, together forming an 18-member municipal council. Ward representation varies: some wards elect two councillors and others elect three, with councillors serving four-year terms under the Ontario Municipal Elections Act.

name: Peterborough
governance_summary: Peterborough voters elect a mayor and 10 city councillors who together form the 11-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each of the city's five wards elects two councillors, with councillors serving four-year terms under Ontario's fixed municipal election cycle.

name: British Columbia
governance_summary: British Columbia voters elect one Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) from each of 93 provincial electoral districts; together the MLAs form the 93-seat Legislative Assembly. The party commanding the confidence of the Assembly forms government, with its leader serving as Premier. Under the Constitution (Fixed Election Dates) Amendment Act, 2001, general elections are held on the third Saturday in October every four years.

name: Norfolk County
governance_summary: Norfolk County voters elect a Mayor county-wide and seven ward councillors (Ward 5 elects two councillors) who together form the eight-member County Council. Each of the seven wards elects at least one councillor to represent that geographic area. The Mayor holds Strong Mayor powers as extended under Ontario legislation effective May 2025.

name: London
governance_summary: London voters elect a Mayor city-wide and 14 Ward Councillors — one per ward — who together form the 15-member City Council. The City of London is a single-tier municipality in Ontario; councillors serve four-year terms and are elected on a non-partisan basis.

name: Waterloo
governance_summary: Waterloo voters elect a mayor and 7 ward councillors who together form the 8-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of 7 wards. Municipal elections are held every 4 years.

name: Oshawa
governance_summary: Oshawa voters elect a mayor and 10 city councillors who together form the 11-member city council. The city is divided into 5 wards; each ward elects one Regional & City Councillor and one City Councillor, both representing that ward. The mayor is elected city-wide.

name: Kingston
governance_summary: Kingston voters elect a mayor at large and 12 district councillors who together form the 13-member city council. Each councillor represents one of 12 geographic districts. Municipal elections are held every four years on the fourth Monday in October.

name: Greater Sudbury
governance_summary: Greater Sudbury voters elect a mayor and 12 ward councillors who together form the 13-member City Council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of 12 wards across this single-tier municipality in northeastern Ontario.

name: Alberta
governance_summary: Alberta voters elect one Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) from each of the province's 87 electoral divisions, forming the unicameral Legislative Assembly of Alberta. Elections are partisan, conducted under single-member plurality, and governed by the fixed-date provision in s.38.1 of the Election Act, which schedules general elections for the third Monday of October in the fourth calendar year following the most recent general election.

name: Calgary
governance_summary: Calgary voters elect a mayor city-wide and 14 city councillors, one representing each of Calgary's 14 wards, together forming the 15-member Calgary City Council. The mayor is elected by all eligible voters across the city; councillors are elected by voters within their individual wards. Both the mayor and councillors hold office for four-year terms under the Local Authorities Election Act.

name: Vancouver
governance_summary: Vancouver voters elect a Mayor and 10 city councillors all city-wide under an at-large system with no wards, as established by the Vancouver Charter. The 11-member council governs on a non-partisan basis; the entire city constitutes a single at-large electoral district.

name: Quebec
governance_summary: Quebec voters elect one Member of the National Assembly (MNA) in each of the province's 125 electoral divisions, forming a unicameral legislature called the Assemblée nationale. Elections are held on the first Monday in October of the fourth year following the previous election, making the next general election fixed for October 5, 2026.

name: Kitchener
governance_summary: Kitchener voters elect a mayor and 10 city councillors who together form the 11-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of 10 wards. Elections are held every four years under the Ontario Municipal Elections Act.

name: Markham
governance_summary: Markham voters elect a mayor, 8 ward councillors, and 4 Regional Councillors who together form city council. Each of the 8 wards elects one city councillor; the 4 Regional Councillors are elected at large across the city and also serve on York Region Council. The mayor is elected city-wide. Elections are held every four years under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act.

name: Vaughan
governance_summary: Vaughan voters elect a mayor, four at-large Local and Regional Councillors, and five ward councillors who together form the ten-member city council. The mayor and Local and Regional Councillors are elected city-wide; each ward councillor represents one of five geographic wards. Elections are held every four years under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act, most recently on October 24, 2022, with the next election scheduled for October 26, 2026.

name: Windsor
governance_summary: Windsor voters elect a mayor city-wide and 10 city councillors who together form the 11-member Windsor City Council. Each councillor represents one of the city's 10 wards, with elections held every four years under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act, most recently on October 24, 2022, with the next election scheduled for October 26, 2026.

name: Richmond Hill
governance_summary: Richmond Hill voters elect a mayor and eight councillors who together form the nine-member city council. Six ward councillors each represent one of six geographic wards; two councillors serve as Regional and Local Councillors elected at large across the municipality. The mayor is elected city-wide. Elections are held every four years under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act.

name: Oakville
governance_summary: Oakville voters elect a mayor and 14 councillors who together form the 15-member Town Council. The mayor is elected town-wide; each of Oakville's 7 wards elects two councillors — one Town Councillor and one Town and Regional Councillor.

name: Burlington
governance_summary: Burlington voters elect a mayor and six city councillors who together form the seven-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of six wards. Elections are held every four years under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act, most recently on October 24, 2022, with the next election day scheduled for October 26, 2026.

name: St. Catharines
governance_summary: St. Catharines voters elect a mayor and 12 city councillors who together form the 13-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each of the city's 6 wards elects 2 councillors.

name: Cambridge
governance_summary: Cambridge voters elect a Mayor city-wide and 8 Ward Councillors — one per ward — who together form City Council. Cambridge is a lower-tier municipality within Waterloo Region; two Regional Councillors are also elected to represent Cambridge at the Regional level.

name: Whitby
governance_summary: Whitby voters elect a mayor and 8 councillors who together form the 9-member Town Council. The mayor is elected town-wide; each of the town's four wards elects one local councillor and one regional councillor (representing Whitby on Durham Regional Council), with all members serving four-year terms under Ontario's fixed municipal election cycle.

name: Ajax
governance_summary: Ajax Town Council consists of a Mayor elected town-wide and six councillors: three Ward Councillors and three Regional Councillors, each representing one of three wards. Together they form the seven-member council. The next municipal election is scheduled for October 26, 2026.

name: Thunder Bay
governance_summary: Thunder Bay voters elect a Mayor city-wide and 12 councillors who together form the 13-member City Council. Seven councillors each represent one of seven geographic wards; five councillors are elected at large to represent the city as a whole.

name: Milton
governance_summary: Milton voters elect a Mayor and eight councillors across four wards, forming a nine-member Town Council. Each ward elects one Town Councillor and one Regional Councillor (who also serves on Halton Regional Council); the Mayor is elected town-wide. Elections are held every four years under Ontario's Municipal Elections Act, with the last election on October 24, 2022, and the next scheduled for October 26, 2026.

name: Nunavut
governance_summary: Nunavut voters elect 22 Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs), one for each of the territory's 22 constituencies, to form the unicameral Legislative Assembly of Nunavut. The territory operates a non-partisan consensus government — there are no political parties; MLAs sit as independents and collectively select the Premier and Cabinet from among themselves.

name: Northwest Territories
governance_summary: The Northwest Territories uses a consensus system of government with no political parties. Voters elect 19 Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) who then collectively select the Premier and Cabinet from among themselves. The Premier serves as head of government and is chosen by the full caucus at the start of each Assembly.

name: Yukon
governance_summary: Yukon voters elect 21 Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) who form the Yukon Legislative Assembly, currently in its 36th sitting. Each MLA represents one of 21 single-member electoral districts; the party commanding the confidence of the Assembly forms government, with its leader serving as Premier.

name: Regina
governance_summary: Regina voters elect a mayor and 10 city councillors who together form the 11-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of 10 wards. Municipal elections are held every four years, most recently on November 13, 2024.

name: Winnipeg
governance_summary: Winnipeg voters elect a Mayor city-wide and one Councillor per ward across 15 wards, together forming the 16-member Winnipeg City Council. Council operates on a non-partisan basis under the City of Winnipeg Charter, which establishes general elections on the fourth Wednesday of October every four years. The most recent general election was held on October 26, 2022, with the next scheduled for October 28, 2026.

name: Prince Edward Island
governance_summary: Prince Edward Island elects 27 Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs), one per electoral district, who together form the unicameral Legislative Assembly of Prince Edward Island. The Premier is the head of government and is the leader of the party that commands a majority in the Assembly. Elections are conducted on a partisan, first-past-the-post basis; the most recent general election was held on April 3, 2024, and the next is scheduled for October 4, 2027.

name: Québec City
governance_summary: Québec City voters elect a mayor and 21 city councillors who together form the 22-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of 21 electoral districts. The council is partisan, with Québec forte et fière holding a majority and Respect citoyens as the official opposition. Elections are held every four years under Quebec municipal law, most recently on November 2, 2025.

name: Newfoundland and Labrador
governance_summary: Newfoundland and Labrador voters elect one Member of the House of Assembly (MHA) from each of the province's 40 electoral districts under first-past-the-post, together forming the unicameral, 40-seat House of Assembly. The party commanding the confidence of the House forms government, with its leader serving as Premier. The most recent general election was held on October 14, 2025, seating the 51st General Assembly; the Elections Act fixed-date provision has applied variably, so no firm next-election date is published.

name: Saskatchewan
governance_summary: Saskatchewan voters elect one Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) from each of the province's 61 single-member constituencies under first-past-the-post; together the MLAs form the Legislative Assembly of Saskatchewan. The party commanding the confidence of the Assembly forms government, with its leader serving as Premier. General elections are held on a fixed four-year cycle on the last Monday of October, most recently in the 29th general election on October 28, 2024, with the next scheduled for October 30, 2028.

name: Victoria
governance_summary: Victoria voters elect a Mayor and 8 city councillors all city-wide under an at-large system with no wards. The 9-member council governs on a non-partisan basis; the entire city constitutes a single at-large electoral district. Elections are held every four years on the provincial general local election day, most recently October 15, 2022, with the next scheduled for October 17, 2026.

name: Edmonton
governance_summary: Edmonton voters elect a mayor and 12 city councillors who together form the 13-member Edmonton City Council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of 12 wards. Elections are held every four years under the Local Authorities Election Act; the most recent election was held on October 20, 2025 and the next is scheduled for October 15, 2029.

name: Manitoba
governance_summary: Manitoba voters elect one Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) from each of the province's 57 single-member electoral divisions under first-past-the-post; together the MLAs form the Legislative Assembly of Manitoba. The party commanding the confidence of the Assembly forms government, with its leader serving as Premier. Under Manitoba's fixed-date provision, general elections are held on the first Tuesday of October in the fourth year following the previous general election, most recently on October 3, 2023, with the next scheduled for October 5, 2027.

name: New Brunswick
governance_summary: New Brunswick voters elect one Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) from each of the province's 49 single-member electoral districts under first-past-the-post; together the MLAs form the Legislative Assembly of New Brunswick. The party commanding the confidence of the Assembly forms government, with its leader serving as Premier. Under the province's fixed-date provision, general elections are held on the third Monday of October in the fourth calendar year following the previous general election; the most recent general election was held on October 21, 2024 (the 41st general election, seating the 61st Assembly), with the next scheduled for October 16, 2028.

name: Nova Scotia
governance_summary: Nova Scotia voters elect one Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) from each of the province's 55 single-member electoral districts under first-past-the-post; together the MLAs form the Nova Scotia House of Assembly. The party commanding the confidence of the House forms government, with its leader serving as Premier. The most recent general election (the 41st) was held on November 26, 2024; the province's fixed-date election law was repealed (royal assent March 26, 2025), so no firm next-election date is published, with the next general election required on or before approximately December 2029.

name: Cornwall
governance_summary: Cornwall voters elect a mayor and six councillors who together form the seven-member town council. All members are elected town-wide through an open ward system; the town is not divided into geographic wards, and one councillor serves as Deputy Mayor.

name: St. John's
governance_summary: St. John's voters elect a mayor, a deputy mayor, and nine councillors who together form the 11-member city council. The mayor and deputy mayor are elected city-wide; five councillors each represent one of five wards and four councillors are elected at-large across the city.

name: Conception Bay South
governance_summary: Conception Bay South voters elect a mayor, four at-large councillors, and four ward councillors, who together form the nine-member Town Council. The mayor and the four at-large councillors are elected town-wide; each ward councillor represents one of the town's four wards. The Deputy Mayor is chosen by Council from among the councillors.

name: Mount Pearl
governance_summary: Mount Pearl voters elect a seven-member city council—a Mayor, a Deputy Mayor, and five Councillors—all elected at-large across the city, which is not divided into wards. Members serve four-year terms under the City of Mount Pearl Act, with elections held the last Tuesday of September every four years.

name: Paradise
governance_summary: Paradise voters elect a mayor and six councillors town-wide who together form the seven-member town council; one councillor serves as deputy mayor. There are no wards; under the town's at-large system every elected official represents the Town of Paradise as a whole. The mayor and councillors were elected in the municipal general election held October 2, 2025 to four-year terms.

name: Corner Brook
governance_summary: Corner Brook voters elect a mayor and six city councillors who together form the seven-member city council. The city operates under an at-large system: the mayor and all councillors are elected city-wide to represent the City as a whole rather than individual wards.

name: Grand Falls-Windsor
governance_summary: Grand Falls-Windsor voters elect a mayor and six councillors town-wide who together form the seven-member town council; one councillor serves as deputy mayor. There are no wards, so all members are elected at large across the town.

name: Gander
governance_summary: Gander voters elect a mayor and six councillors who together form the seven-member town council. Both the mayor and all councillors are elected town-wide (at-large); the town is not divided into wards, and the deputy mayor is chosen by a vote of council from among the elected councillors.

name: Portugal Cove-St. Philip's
governance_summary: Portugal Cove-St. Philip's voters elect a mayor and up to six councillors, all elected town-wide rather than by ward; together they form the town council. The Deputy Mayor is selected by the newly elected council from among the councillors. The most recent municipal general election was held October 2, 2025, for a four-year term.

name: Happy Valley-Goose Bay
governance_summary: Happy Valley-Goose Bay voters elect a mayor, a deputy mayor, and five councillors who together form the seven-member town council. All members are elected town-wide at-large rather than by ward, under Newfoundland and Labrador's Municipal Elections Act, serving four-year terms.

name: Torbay
governance_summary: Torbay voters elect a mayor, a deputy mayor, and five councillors who together form the seven-member town council. All members are elected at-large town-wide rather than by ward, under the Newfoundland and Labrador Municipalities Act.

name: Moncton
governance_summary: Moncton voters elect a mayor, two at-large councillors, and eight ward councillors who together form the 11-member city council. The city is divided into four wards, each represented by two ward councillors; the mayor and the two at-large councillors are elected city-wide. Elections are non-partisan and held on New Brunswick's fixed four-year municipal cycle.

name: Saint John
governance_summary: Saint John voters elect a mayor and 10 councillors who together form the 11-member Common Council. The mayor and two councillors are elected city-wide (at large); the remaining eight councillors represent the city's four wards, with two councillors elected per ward.

name: Fredericton
governance_summary: Fredericton voters elect a mayor and 12 city councillors who together form the 13-member city council. The mayor is elected at large; each councillor represents one of the city’s 12 wards.

name: Dieppe
governance_summary: Dieppe voters elect a mayor, three councillors-at-large, and five ward councillors who together form the nine-member city council. The mayor and the three councillors-at-large are elected city-wide; each of the five ward councillors represents one of the city's five wards. The council was elected at the New Brunswick local government general election of May 11, 2026, under the structure established by the 2023 local governance reform, and serves a four-year term.

name: Riverview
governance_summary: Riverview voters elect a mayor and seven town councillors who together form the eight-member town council. Four councillors each represent one of the town's four wards, and three councillors are elected at large across the whole town; the mayor is elected town-wide. Councillors serve four-year terms.

name: Regional Municipality of Tracadie
governance_summary: The Regional Municipality of Tracadie — the first and only regional municipality in New Brunswick, established under the Local Governance Act — is governed by a non-partisan council of a mayor and 10 councillors representing 8 wards. The mayor is elected municipality-wide; six rural wards (1–6) each elect one councillor while wards 7 and 8 each elect two, for a 11-member council.

name: Edmundston
governance_summary: Edmundston voters elect a mayor and nine city councillors who together form the 10-member city council. The mayor is elected at-large by universal suffrage; each of the three electoral wards elects three councillors. The current council was sworn in on June 2, 2026 following the May 11, 2026 municipal election and serves a four-year term.

name: Quispamsis
governance_summary: Quispamsis voters elect a mayor and seven councillors who together form the eight-member town council. All members are elected at large town-wide; the town has no wards, and the deputy mayor is selected by council from among the councillors.

name: Miramichi
governance_summary: Miramichi voters elect a mayor and eight city councillors who together form the nine-member city council. All are elected at-large city-wide; the city has no wards, and one councillor serves as Deputy Mayor.

name: Bathurst
governance_summary: Bathurst voters elect a mayor and 9 city councillors who together form the 10-member city council. All council positions are elected at large across the whole city; one councillor serves a one-year term as Deputy Mayor. Members serve four-year terms.

name: Halifax
governance_summary: Halifax Regional Municipality voters elect a mayor and 16 councillors who together form the 17-member Regional Council. The mayor is elected municipality-wide; each councillor represents one of 16 districts.

name: Cape Breton Regional Municipality
governance_summary: Cape Breton Regional Municipality voters elect a mayor and 12 district councillors who together form the 13-member Regional Council. The mayor is elected at-large across the municipality; each councillor represents one of 12 electoral districts. Elections are held every four years on a non-partisan basis.

name: Municipality of the County of Kings
governance_summary: Voters in the Municipality of the County of Kings elect a mayor and nine district councillors who together form the 10-member municipal council. The mayor is elected at-large by all nine districts; each councillor represents one of the nine electoral districts. The non-partisan council serves a four-year term, with the current term running 2024-2028.

name: Municipality of the County of Colchester
governance_summary: Colchester voters elect a mayor and 11 district councillors who together form the 12-member municipal council. The mayor is elected at-large across the county; each councillor represents one of 11 electoral districts. Council is non-partisan and serves four-year terms; the most recent general election was held October 19, 2024.

name: Municipality of East Hants
governance_summary: East Hants voters elect 11 councillors, one for each of the municipality's 11 single-member districts, who together form the 11-member council. The council's head of government is the Warden, chosen from among the councillors; the Warden continues to represent their own district seat. The most recent municipal general election was held October 19, 2024 for four-year terms.

name: Municipality of the County of Pictou
governance_summary: Voters in the Municipality of the County of Pictou elect 12 councillors, one for each of the 12 single-member districts, who together form the 12-member municipal council. The council chooses a Warden (and Deputy Warden) by ballot from among the elected councillors to serve as head of council; the Warden continues to hold their own district seat.

name: Municipality of the County of Cumberland
governance_summary: Voters in the Municipality of the County of Cumberland elect a mayor and eight district councillors who together form the nine-member municipal council. The mayor is elected at-large (a directly elected mayor since 2020, replacing the former warden system); each councillor represents one of eight single-member districts. Municipal elections are non-partisan and held on a four-year cycle.

name: West Hants Regional Municipality
governance_summary: West Hants Regional Municipality voters elect a mayor and 11 councillors who together form a 12-member council. The mayor is elected at-large across the municipality; each councillor represents one of 11 districts. The municipality was formed in 2020 through the amalgamation of the Town of Windsor and the District of West Hants, and councillors serve four-year terms.

name: Municipality of the County of Annapolis
governance_summary: Voters in the Municipality of the County of Annapolis elect 11 councillors, one from each of 11 single-member electoral districts, who together form the 11-member municipal council. The council selects a Warden (head of government) and a Deputy Warden from among its own members; the Warden continues to hold their district seat. The government is non-partisan and councillors serve four-year terms.

name: Steinbach
governance_summary: Steinbach voters elect a mayor and six councillors who together form the seven-member city council. All members are elected at-large across the city; Steinbach has no wards. General municipal elections are held every four years on the fourth Wednesday in October.

name: Winkler
governance_summary: Winkler voters elect a mayor and five city councillors who together form the seven-member city council, including a deputy mayor chosen from among the councillors. All members are elected city-wide at large; the city has no wards.

name: Portage la Prairie
governance_summary: Portage la Prairie voters elect a mayor and 6 city councillors who together form the 7-member city council. The mayor and all councillors are elected at-large city-wide; the city has no wards.

name: Thompson
governance_summary: Thompson voters elect a mayor and 8 councillors city-wide who together form the 9-member city council, governed under The Thompson Charter Act. The city has no wards; all members are elected at-large, with one councillor designated Deputy Mayor.

name: Selkirk
governance_summary: Selkirk voters elect a mayor and six city councillors who together form the seven-member city council. The city is not divided into wards: the mayor and all six councillors are elected at-large, so every member of council represents all residents of the city.

name: Morden
governance_summary: Morden voters elect a mayor and six councillors, all elected at-large across the city; there are no wards. The mayor and the six councillors together form Morden's seven-member city council, which is non-partisan and serves a four-year term under Manitoba's Municipal Councils and School Boards Elections Act.

name: Saskatoon
governance_summary: Saskatoon voters elect a mayor and 10 city councillors who together form the 11-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of the city's 10 wards. The council serves a four-year term under Saskatchewan's The Cities Act, with the most recent civic election held in November 2024 and the next scheduled for November 2028.

name: Prince Albert
governance_summary: Prince Albert voters elect a mayor and eight city councillors who together form the nine-member city council. The mayor is elected at-large; each councillor represents one of eight wards. Elections are held every four years and are non-partisan.

name: Moose Jaw
governance_summary: Moose Jaw voters elect a mayor and 6 city councillors who together form the 7-member city council. All members are elected at-large city-wide; the city has no ward system. The mayor and councillors serve four-year terms, most recently elected on November 13, 2024.

name: Swift Current
governance_summary: Swift Current voters elect a mayor and 6 councillors who together form the 7-member city council. The mayor and all councillors are elected at-large across the city; there are no wards. Council serves a four-year term (current term 2024–2028); Saskatchewan municipal general elections are held province-wide every four years under The Local Government Election Act, 2015.

name: Yorkton
governance_summary: Yorkton voters elect a mayor and six city councillors who together form the seven-member city council. All members are elected at-large city-wide; the city is not divided into wards. Council members serve four-year terms, with the current council elected November 13, 2024.

name: North Battleford
governance_summary: North Battleford voters elect a mayor and six city councillors who together form the seven-member city council. All seven are elected at-large city-wide rather than by ward; voters cast one vote for mayor and up to six councillor votes. Council is non-partisan and serves a four-year term, most recently elected in the November 13, 2024 municipal election.

name: Warman
governance_summary: Warman voters elect a mayor and six city councillors who together form the seven-member city council. All members are elected at-large city-wide; the city is not divided into wards. Council serves a four-year term and is governed under Saskatchewan's The Cities Act and The Local Government Election Act.

name: Lloydminster
governance_summary: Lloydminster voters elect a mayor and six city councillors who together form the seven-member city council; all are elected at-large city-wide, as the city has no wards. Lloydminster straddles the Alberta–Saskatchewan border and is governed as a single city under The Lloydminster Charter, registered once under Saskatchewan.

name: Weyburn
governance_summary: Weyburn voters elect a mayor and six city councillors who together form the seven-member city council. All are elected at-large across the entire city; there are no wards. Municipal elections are non-partisan and held every four years under Saskatchewan's Local Government Election Act, most recently on November 13, 2024.

name: Red Deer
governance_summary: Red Deer voters elect a mayor and 8 city councillors who together form the 9-member city council. All members are elected at-large city-wide; the city has no wards.

name: Strathcona County
governance_summary: Strathcona County is a specialized municipality in Alberta that includes the urban service area of Sherwood Park. Voters elect a mayor and eight councillors who together form the nine-member County Council. The mayor is elected at-large, while each councillor represents one of the County's eight wards.

name: Lethbridge
governance_summary: Lethbridge voters elect a mayor and 8 city councillors who together form the 9-member city council. The mayor and all councillors are elected city-wide (at large); Lethbridge has no wards. Members serve four-year terms; the most recent election was held October 20, 2025.

name: Airdrie
governance_summary: Airdrie voters elect a full-time Mayor and six part-time Councillors who together form the seven-member City Council. All members are elected at-large city-wide; the city is not divided into wards.

name: St. Albert
governance_summary: St. Albert voters elect a mayor and six city councillors who together form the seven-member city council. All seven are elected at-large city-wide; the city is not divided into wards.

name: Grande Prairie
governance_summary: Grande Prairie voters elect a mayor and eight city councillors who together form the nine-member city council. All members are elected at-large city-wide; there are no wards. Council serves a four-year term following the October 20, 2025 municipal election, with the next general municipal election scheduled for 2029 under Alberta's Local Authorities Election Act.

name: Medicine Hat
governance_summary: Medicine Hat voters elect a mayor and eight city councillors who together form the nine-member city council. All are elected at-large city-wide rather than by ward; the most recent municipal election was held October 20, 2025 for a four-year term.

name: Surrey
governance_summary: Surrey voters elect a mayor and 8 city councillors who together form the 9-member city council. Both the mayor and all councillors are elected at-large across the entire city rather than by ward.

name: Burnaby
governance_summary: Burnaby voters elect a mayor and eight city councillors who together form the nine-member city council. All are elected at-large city-wide; Burnaby has no wards.

name: Richmond
governance_summary: Richmond voters elect a mayor and eight city councillors who together form the nine-member city council. All members are elected at large city-wide; the city is not divided into wards.

name: Abbotsford
governance_summary: Abbotsford voters elect a mayor and 8 city councillors who together form the 9-member city council. All members are elected at-large city-wide; the city is not divided into wards.

name: Coquitlam
governance_summary: Coquitlam voters elect a mayor and eight city councillors who together form the nine-member city council. All are elected at-large city-wide rather than by ward, for four-year terms under British Columbia's Local Government Act and Community Charter.

name: Kelowna
governance_summary: Kelowna voters elect a mayor and eight city councillors who together form the nine-member city council. The mayor and all councillors are elected at large city-wide; there are no wards.

name: Township of Langley
governance_summary: Township of Langley voters elect a Mayor and eight Councillors who together form the nine-member municipal Council. All members are elected at-large across the entire municipality rather than by ward, and serve four-year terms.

name: Saanich
governance_summary: Saanich voters elect a mayor and eight councillors who together form the nine-member municipal council. All members are elected at-large across the entire municipality rather than by ward, and serve four-year terms under British Columbia's Community Charter and Local Government Act.

name: Montréal
governance_summary: Montréal voters elect a mayor city-wide plus a multi-tiered council: 46 city councillors and 38 borough councillors elected by district across 58 electoral districts, and 18 borough mayors elected borough-wide. The 65-member city council (mayor plus 64) and 19 borough councils govern the partisan municipality; a comité exécutif of about 20 members acts as the executive.

name: Laval
governance_summary: Laval voters elect a mayor city-wide and 22 city councillors who together form the 23-member city council; each councillor represents one of the city's 22 districts. Unlike most Canadian municipalities, Laval's politics are partisan, organized around municipal parties such as the Mouvement lavallois.

name: Gatineau
governance_summary: Gatineau voters elect a mayor and 19 city councillors who together form the 20-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of 19 electoral districts. Unlike most Canadian municipalities, Gatineau's politics are partisan, with Action Gatineau holding a council majority following the November 2, 2025 election (2025-2029 term).

name: Longueuil
governance_summary: Longueuil voters elect a mayor city-wide and 18 district councillors who together form the city council (la mairesse et 18 conseillères et conseillers). Municipal politics in Longueuil is partisan; in the 2 November 2025 election the Coalition Longueuil party, led by mayor Catherine Fournier, won the mayoralty and every council district. The city is further divided into three boroughs (arrondissements): Le Vieux-Longueuil, Saint-Hubert, and Greenfield Park.

name: Sherbrooke
governance_summary: Sherbrooke voters elect a mayor (mairesse) city-wide and 16 district councillors who together form the city council. The city is organized into four arrondissements (boroughs); each councillor represents one electoral district. Although registered municipal parties exist, the council elected in 2025 is composed mostly of independents.

name: Trois-Rivières
governance_summary: Trois-Rivières voters elect a mayor and 14 city councillors who together form the 15-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of the city's 14 electoral districts.

name: Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu
governance_summary: Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu voters elect a mayor city-wide and 12 councillors who together form the 13-member municipal council; each councillor represents one of the city's 12 electoral districts. Unlike most Canadian municipalities, the council is partisan, organized around party slates — Mayor Éric Latour leads the Coalition Éric Latour. Members serve four-year terms following the Quebec general municipal election held province-wide on the first Sunday of November.

name: Repentigny
governance_summary: Repentigny voters elect a mayor and 12 city councillors who together form the 13-member city council. The mayor is elected city-wide; each councillor represents one of 12 electoral districts. Municipal politics in Repentigny are partisan: the party Avenir Repentigny - Équipe Nicolas Dufour holds the mayoralty and all 12 district seats following the 2025 election.

name: Brandon
governance_summary: Brandon voters elect a Mayor city-wide and one Councillor per ward across 10 wards, together forming the 11-member Brandon City Council. Council operates on a non-partisan basis under Manitoba's Municipal Councils and School Boards Elections Act, which sets general elections on the fourth Wednesday of October every four years. The most recent general election was held on October 26, 2022, with the next scheduled for October 28, 2026.
